claims.text: The as-processed HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a high-disorder solid solution.
Heating HfNbTaTiZr to elevated temperatures changes its local lattice distortions.
Heating HfNbTaTiZr to elevated temperatures changes its short-range chemical order.
At elevated temperatures, lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr increase.
The evolution of lattice distortion and short-range chemical order produces a microstructural transition in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed microstructural transition shifts the dominant dislocation mechanism from screw to edge dislocations.
The change in dislocation dynamics causes anomalous stress-strain behavior in HfNbTaTiZr.
The change in dislocation dynamics causes irregular thermal expansion in HfNbTaTiZr.
The change in dislocation dynamics causes deviations in the elastic modulus of HfNbTaTiZr.
Between 600°C and 1200°C, HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit greater strain hardening than a conventional lower-entropy alloy tested under identical conditions.
Between 600°C and 1200°C, HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit a nonlinear temperature-dependent change in lattice parameters relative to the lower-entropy reference alloy.
The nonlinear lattice-parameter change is indicative of anomalous thermal expansion.
Between 600°C and 1200°C, HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit elastic moduli different from those of the lower-entropy reference alloy.
Diffraction measurements will reveal a microstructural-transition signature corresponding to a change in dislocation behavior.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply only from approximately 600°C to 1200°C and within the elastic and early plastic deformation regimes.
Outside the stated temperature and deformation limits, other mechanisms may dominate the response.
Previous studies indicate that local lattice distortions and short-range order affect high-entropy alloys.
